items.hed: With less than 48 hours to go before Thursday night's kickoff at Indianapolis, Houston's clearest injury-report news stays David Montgomery trending toward a return after four missed games, while rookie back Woody Marks is dealing with a concussion from Sunday's loss to Cleveland
items.insight: The Texans' Monday injury report, the most recent available ahead of the short week, estimated Montgomery as a full participant for a second straight day, putting him on track to play Thursday after a groin injury had sidelined him since late October, according to a Houston beat report. The same report listed linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair, receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., defensive end Danielle Hunter, tight end Brevin Jordan and Marks as non-participants, with linebacker Jake Hummel limited; all five missed Sunday's game, and Houston's practice schedule for a Thursday game leaves little time to add a fresher report before kickoff.
items.image_caption: NRG Stadium, Houston, Feb. 5, 2017. Venue still.

items.hed: Houston's 40-man roster deadline for the Rule 5 Draft arrives tonight at 6 p.m. ET, the hour by which the Astros must add any prospect they want to protect or risk losing him to another club in December
items.insight: All 30 clubs face the same evening deadline to add Rule 5-eligible players to their 40-man rosters ahead of the Rule 5 Draft at December's Winter Meetings in San Diego, according to MLB.com, with right-hander James Hicks — the 2025 Arizona Fall League Pitcher of the Year — among the Astros prospects MLB.com's prospect staff flagged as a notable bubble call heading into tonight's cutoff. MLB.com's reporting also lists eight Top-100 prospects league-wide who are expected to be protected, with many other close roster calls still being decided as the deadline closes in.
items.image_caption: NRG Stadium, Houston, Feb. 5, 2017. Venue still (page hero shared across today's Texas desk; Astros are in their off-season).

items.hed: Rockets guard Amen Thompson sat out the second half of a back-to-back with a knee issue, and big man Jabari Smith Jr. answered with his third double-double of the season filling in
items.insight: Smith's double-double was his first since a Nov. 2 win over Boston, after he had cooled off from a hot October stretch in which he averaged 11.9 points and 7.1 rebounds per game this month, according to NBA.com's own team fantasy notes. The team report credited Smith and backup guard Reed Sheppard with carrying extra minutes while Houston worked around Thompson's absence, though Sheppard remained limited to a reserve role.
